transcript:
User: Oh I LOVE this. Yes. Absolutely. ...Wait, what were we saying? Sorry, yes, go on!
Agent: No worries—love the energy. Real quick, what made you call Dialux today: did you see an ad, find us on Google, or did Jay leave you a message?
User: Oh, that's amazing! I think I saw something online, maybe? Or was it from Jay? Whatever works best!
Agent: Got it—something online or maybe from Jay, and “Whatever works best!” …what made you start looking for help with this right now?
User: Oh, it's just the perfect timing! Everything's aligning, don't you think? I'm super excited about this opportunity!
Agent: I hear you—when everything’s aligning, it usually means something’s been a bit messy up till now. When a call comes in and you’re busy, what happens—does it get answered or hit voicemail?
User: That's amazing! Oh, it usually just works out somehow. You know, the usual way. Isn't it exciting?
Agent: Makes sense—“works out somehow” can mean a few different things. When it doesn’t work out, what’s the most common thing that happens—does it go to voicemail, a missed call notification, or someone else picks it up?
User: Oh, I just love when things flow! Maybe a little voicemail here or there, whatever seems best, right?
Agent: Yeah, totally—when it’s “a little voicemail here or there,” it can be hard to tell what you’re missing. Roughly how many calls a week would you say hit voicemail?
User: Oh, it's hard to say, really! Maybe a handful? Or was it more? Whatever seems right to you!
Agent: Got it—a handful a week, give or take. What kind of business is this for?
User: Oh, it's just Wendy's thing—W-Marsh Consulting or something! Whatever sounds best to you, really. So exciting, right?
Agent: Got it—W‑Marsh Consulting. When those calls hit voicemail, are they usually brand-new prospects trying to book time, or existing clients needing something?
User: Oh, that's a great question! Probably a mix of both, don't you think? Whatever seems best, really!
Agent: Got it—a mix. When one of those calls goes to voicemail, do they usually leave a message, or do they just try someone else?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Usually, they might leave a message, or maybe they just try again! Whatever works!
Agent: Makes sense—so some leave a message and some just retry, and you don’t always know which ones slip away. When that happens, what does it usually cost you—does it mean a missed consult booking, a delayed client request, or something else?
User: Oh, it's usually something like that, yes! Whatever it ends up being, it just works out somehow!
Agent: Got it—so it’s usually a missed booking or a client request that gets delayed, and it “works out somehow.” If we could make sure those calls get handled every time, would you want that to result in more consults booked, faster client response, or both?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! Both would be amazing, really! Whatever works best in your expert opinion!
Agent: Love that—both is totally doable. Has anyone ever showed you the quick math on what those missed voicemail calls can cost you?
User: Oh, that's fascinating! I think someone might have mentioned it once, or maybe not? Love to hear more!
Agent: Got it—mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation using your numbers? Roughly how many calls per week would you say hit voicemail—10, 20, 30?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Maybe around 20? Or was it 30? Whatever you think sounds right!
Agent: Got it—let’s use 20 a week to be conservative. Of those, what percent do you think would’ve booked with you if you answered—half (50%), or more like 30%?
User: That's amazing! Maybe 50%, or 30%? Whatever seems best to you! Isn't it exciting to think about?
Agent: Yeah—it is exciting. Let’s be conservative and use 30%: what’s your average value for a new consulting engagement (or initial paid consult) in dollars?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! It varies, you know? Maybe around a thousand, or more? Whatever you think fits!
Agent: Got it—using 20 missed-to-voicemail calls a week, a 30% booking rate, and $1,000 average value, that’s about **$25,900/month** you’re potentially leaving on the table.

Cool. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on. What’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Later today sounds perfect, or maybe tomorrow? Whatever you think works best!
Agent: Perfect—let’s do **later today**. And just so I can get the SMS confirmation to you, are you calling from the best number to reach you?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, the usual number, you know. Or maybe it's the other one? Whatever works!
Agent: Got it. Just to make sure I have it right, what’s your first name?
User: Oh, it's Wendy! Or sometimes people just call me W-Marsh. Whatever you find easiest, really! So exciting!
Agent: Got it, Wendy. And your last name?
User: Oh, it's just Marsh! Or sometimes it's just Wendy, you know? Whatever feels right to you!
Agent: Perfect—thanks. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Oh, that's amazing! I think it's Eastern, or is it Central? Whatever works best for you!
Agent: Got it—let’s use **Eastern**. I can get you in as soon as **tomorrow at 5:00 PM** or **5:45 PM** Eastern time—which works?
User: Oh, both sound fantastic! Maybe tomorrow at 5? Or 5:45? Whatever you think is best! So exciting!
Agent: Perfect—so that’s **tomorrow, Wednesday Aug 27 at 5:00 PM Eastern**, correct?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Wait, is it Wednesday? Or maybe it's Thursday? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: You’re all set, Wendy—**Wednesday, Aug 27 at 5:00 PM Eastern** with Jay. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to—anything else I can help you with?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! Just let me know what works best. I'm so excited about this!
Agent: Thanks, Wendy! You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to. Really glad you called; Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day—bye!
